messages:
Maya (PM): Heads-up — planning huddle for Q3 hosted serving slices. Focus: embedding latency budget, rerank pipeline throughput, and canary/launch must-haves. Quick sync tomorrow 10am PT? Context: 3 pilot customers asking for 99p <= 120ms for 512-dim embeddings, and rerank target ~200 qps. Need to align on scope and tradeoffs.
Noah (Eng): High-level triage: 120ms p99 for 512s is doable but expensive. Options: per-tenant warm pools + prefix cache (predictable but infra cost), or smaller embed model (quantized / distilled) with lower quality. Which do we lean to?
Liam (SRE): Warm pools add complexity but give predictable p95/p99. We can prototype a dynamic prewarm autoscaler, but we need to measure cold-start profile. Also: is 99p 120ms expected globally or per-region? Routing plan depends on that.
Maya (PM): For pilots they want global SLA ideally. For initial launch we can accept region-level per-tenant SLAs. Can Hosted API support region pinning or per-tenant routing configs? @Noah
Noah (Eng): Region pinning is supported in Dedicated. For Hosted we need a routing policy change + fallback path to a cheaper model. Proposal: route requests by latency SLO; when we can't meet it, fallback to `embed-lite` and tag the response. Also expose `served_model` in response metadata so customers can detect fallbacks.
Sophia (Product): From UX perspective, keep flags minimal. Expose `served_model` and `served_at` and a simple `latency_hint`. Must call out billing delta clearly in docs (embed-lite cheaper).
Eva (ML): Quality note: embed-lite causes ~6-8% drop in retrieval recall in our evals (on our standard dev sets). For pilots with strict recall needs, warm pools + quantized full model is preferred. Suggest hybrid: prefer warm pools, fallback to embed-lite only under capacity pressure.
Maya (PM): Decision proposal: prioritize warm-pool autoscaler as Q3 MVP; implement runtime fallback to embed-lite + metadata tagging; update docs and billing transparency. OKRs: GA target p99 <= 150ms for 512-dim, but aim for 120ms for pilot tenants. Reasonable?
Noah (Eng): I can take the autoscaler spike (2w) + routing policy change (1w). Need an infra ticket and a canary plan. Canary idea: 5% traffic with hot-prefix memcache for 48h, then 25% if stable.
Liam (SRE): I'll own runbook + rollback. Canary checks: p99 latency, error rate, OOMs, cost-per-request spike. Also need alerts for fallback-rate > 5%.
Maya (PM): Action items: @Noah create RFC + infra tickets by EOD Friday; @Liam draft runbook; @Sophia update customer-facing docs; @Eva assemble recall eval comparing embed-lite vs full model by next Wed. We'll review in tomorrow's sync. :thumbsup:
